paper.title: A Survey on Contextual Multi-armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Reduce to K-armed bandits (finite context set, policies = all mappings from contexts to arms)
unmapped: finite set of M_ctx = C distinct contexts, enumerable
settings.definition_quote: Suppose there are $C$ distinct contexts in the context set $\mathcal{X}$, and the context at time $t$ is $x_t \in \{1, 2, ..., C\}$. ... Define the policy set to be all the possible mappings from contexts to arms as $\Pi = \{f: \mathcal{X} \rightarrow \mathcal{A}\}$, then the regret of the agent is defined as: R_T = \sup_{f\in \Pi} \mathrm{E}[ \sum_{t=1}^T(r_{t, f(x_t)} - r_{t, a_t}) ]

algorithms.name: EXP3 applied independently on each context

tuning: EXP3 tuned as in Auer et al. (2002) per context

source.quote: Apply EXP3 \citep{auer2002nonstochastic}, a non-contextual multi-armed bandits algorithm, on each context, then the regret is R_T \le 2.63\sqrt{TCK\ln K}

results.notes: Survey's own simple derivation (folklore). Paper's C = number of contexts (M_ctx). Regret defined as sup over policies of expectation. Table says T must be known.
